Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage across major business and general-news outlets this weekend is dominated by the fallout from the US midterm elections, specifically the historic sell-off and partial recovery in AI and tech stocks as investors reassess the data-center buildout under incoming Democratic state leadership. Secondary threads include Berkshire Hathaway's blockbuster earnings as a market safe-haven, the Fox-Roku streaming merger, and fresh Nvidia-related controversies.

stories.headline: AI Stock Rout Rattles Wall Street After Midterm Sweep
stories.summary: The Nasdaq suffered its worst day since the 2025 tariff panic as Democratic wins in data-center-heavy states like Ohio, Georgia and Texas fueled fears of moratoriums on AI infrastructure, with chipmakers, neoclouds and industrial suppliers tied to the buildout hit hardest before stocks partially recovered Friday.

stories.headline: Berkshire Hathaway Boosts Buybacks as Operating Income Slips
stories.summary: Berkshire Hathaway repurchased about $9.6 billion of its own stock in the third quarter, more than double the prior quarter's pace, even as operating earnings fell 5.8% on weaker insurance underwriting and investment income; the conglomerate's shares have become a haven as investors flee the AI-stock turmoil.

stories.headline: Nvidia Seeks Workaround to Data-Center Backlash by Retrofitting Old Phone Buildings
stories.summary: Nvidia has approached private equity firm Apollo Global Management about building a network of small AI data centers across roughly 20 states using existing telecom buildings, a response to mounting local political opposition after the midterms.

stories.headline: Fox Closes $22 Billion Deal to Buy Roku
stories.summary: Fox has completed its $22 billion acquisition of Roku, a deal the Post says will reshape the streaming landscape by giving Fox a major edge in free, ad-supported video.

stories.headline: US Cleared Nvidia Chips to Chinese Firms With Empty Offices and Troubling Ties
stories.summary: The Commerce Department approved dozens of Chinese companies to handle Nvidia's H200 chips, and the New York Times reports some of those firms have ties to entities already under US national-security sanctions.

stories.headline: US Believes Nvidia's Huang Had Romantic Relationship With Alleged Chinese Spy
stories.summary: The Financial Times reports American intelligence officials warned that Nvidia chief Jensen Huang had been involved with an executive allegedly recruited by China to gather information on the company.

stories.headline: Paraguay's President Removed and Arrested Over Financial Crisis
stories.summary: Santiago Peña was impeached, removed from office and placed under house arrest after a bank closely tied to his administration collapsed, according to the New York Times.

stories.headline: Tesla to Wind Down Cybertruck Production in Texas
stories.summary: Elon Musk said Tesla will phase out Cybertruck production next year to make room for the autonomous Cybercab, after the polarizing vehicle failed to reach mass-market sales despite several recalls.

Business.gaps: Forbes and Puck had no fresh business-relevant stories in the last 24-48 hours beyond fashion/media-industry coverage already several days old; WSJ, NYT, FT, Economist, Politico and BBC coverage is limited to what appeared in the provided feed items since these outlets could not be searched directly.

US politics.overview: Coverage across these outlets is dominated by the fallout from Tuesday's historic Democratic midterm sweep, especially Trump's decision to replace Susie Wiles with hardliner Stephen Miller as chief of staff, GOP infighting and recrimination, and what a Democratic-controlled Congress means for judicial confirmations, SCOTUS, and Trump's final two years. Secondary threads include market jitters over AI investment tied to the election results and down-ballot stories like Mississippi's historic Senate race and Texas's blue shift.

stories.headline: Trump replaces Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as chief of staff
stories.summary: Axios reports that an angered Trump replaced Wiles with Stephen Miller after the midterm losses, trading one of his moderating forces for a hardline immigration and Iran-war advocate, in what Axios calls a signal Trump may double down on the policies that just cost Republicans Congress.

stories.headline: House GOP erupts at Miller's promotion, calling it a 'megalomaniac' move
stories.summary: Fox News reports that multiple House Republicans are fuming over Miller's elevation, with lawmakers like Rep. Marlin Stutzman calling it a 'horrible decision' and retiring Rep. Don Bacon saying Miller 'greatly hurt the administration and cost us many seats.'

stories.headline: GOP reckoning deepens after 'historic' midterm defeat
stories.summary: Politico reports that Stephen Miller's rise has exacerbated Republican fears there will be no party-wide reckoning after the midterm wipeout, with Oklahoma Gov. Kevin Stitt blaming a lack of 'civility' from Trump for the losses.

stories.headline: Democratic Senate win ends Trump's glide path on judicial confirmations
stories.summary: The Hill reports that Democrats' Senate takeover means Trump will for the first time lose his glide path to confirm judges and Supreme Court justices, intensifying pressure on aging conservative justices.

stories.headline: GOP's lame-duck Congress races the clock on NDAA, funding before Democrats take over
stories.summary: NPR reports that the outgoing Republican-led Congress must still pass the National Defense Authorization Act and a government funding bill before Democrats take control on Jan. 3.

stories.headline: Investors dump AI stocks on fears Democratic sweep will slow data-center buildout
stories.summary: The Washington Post reports investors worry Democrats' election wins could slow data-center construction, with Asian and European markets sliding Friday as the AI-investment math comes under new scrutiny.

stories.headline: Scott Colom's Mississippi Senate bid nears historic finish as count continues
stories.summary: Courthouse News reports that as ballots are still being counted in Mississippi's Senate race, Democrat Scott Colom's candidacy has taken on historic significance for Black voters in the state.

stories.headline: Longtime West Virginia Sen. Jay Rockefeller dies
stories.summary: Roll Call reports the death of former longtime West Virginia Democratic Sen. John D. Rockefeller IV.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS, Cook Political Report, and Punchbowl News appeared mostly via older cached/search-indexed items rather than fresh last-24-48-hour posts; their most recent visible items (e.g., Cook's pre-election ratings, NOTUS's Congress page) predate this reporting window, so only limited current-cycle content could be confirmed. SCOTUSblog, Stateline, and National Review had relevant midterm-aftermath pieces but no additional distinct top story beyond what's listed.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across these outlets is dominated by the fallout from this week's AI-stock selloff tied to the Democratic midterm sweep, parallel multibillion-dollar fundraising moves by OpenAI and Anthropic, and a cluster of national-security stories involving Nvidia's chip exports to China and alleged espionage touching CEO Jensen Huang. A steady drumbeat of AI-related cybersecurity incidents (Chainalysis, Artex, Claude flaws) also features prominently.

stories.headline: Anthropic Files S-1, Presses Ahead With Pre-Thanksgiving IPO Despite Tech Selloff
stories.summary: Anthropic is moving ahead with an IPO roadshow before Thanksgiving at a trimmed valuation of $1.25 to $1.75 trillion, well below its earlier $2 trillion target, after formally filing a registration statement for the offering. Anthropic's own newsroom confirms that today, Anthropic, PBC filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission relating to its proposed initial public offering.

stories.headline: OpenAI Raises $11 Billion at $1.25 Trillion Valuation
stories.summary: OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11 billion as part of a funding round that hasn't closed yet but is expected to in the coming weeks, with The Information reporting the company has so far raised just over half of its new target for the fundraising round and plans to brief investors next week.

stories.headline: US Cleared Nvidia Chips for Chinese Firms With Empty Offices and Sanctioned Ties
stories.summary: An investigation found the Commerce Department has approved dozens of Chinese companies to handle Nvidia's H200 chips, some with empty offices and ties to firms under sanctions, raising questions about export-control vetting.

stories.headline: The Wild Week That Brought AI Investors to the Brink
stories.summary: Democrats' sweeping midterm wins intensified investor anxiety that had been building around the AI trade, and systematic trading strategies then amplified the resulting losses across tech stocks.

stories.headline: US Believes Nvidia's Huang Had Romantic Relationship With Alleged Chinese Spy
stories.summary: American intelligence officials reportedly warned that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was involved with an executive recruited by China to gather information on the chipmaker; separately, three House committees have requested a briefing with Huang citing national security concerns.

stories.headline: Chainalysis Says Hackers Stole Credentials and Tokens for All of Its Customers
stories.summary: The blockchain analytics firm disclosed a multifront cyberattack, which it says involved AI agents, that resulted in the theft of credentials and tokens across its entire customer base.

stories.headline: Hundreds of Artex AI Hacking Tools Found Publicly Exposed to the Web
stories.summary: Security researchers found hundreds of servers hosting Artex, a Chinese-made AI-powered penetration-testing tool linked to several cyberattacks since July, left openly accessible on the internet.

stories.headline: OpenAI's Disproof of a Major Computer Science Conjecture Stuns Theorists
stories.summary: Theoretical computer scientist Russell Impagliazzo, a co-proposer of the Exponential Time Hypothesis, called OpenAI's disproof of the conjecture 'shocking,' with implications that could one day speed up chip design and break current encryption.

Tech & AI.gaps: Platformer and Rest of World had no retrievable recent coverage within search limits for this cycle. Google DeepMind's own newsroom showed only routine product listings (Genie 4, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash) without a distinct breaking story in the last 48 hours.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are dominated by fallout from the U.S. midterm elections, where data-center backlash and rising electricity bills drove a Democratic sweep that could reshape state and federal energy policy. Secondary threads include utilities reaffirming massive capex plans despite the political shift, a historic rate-hike request in California, and climate science stories on a 'super El Niño' and China's falling emissions.

stories.headline: Democrats' midterm sweep set to rewire energy and data-center policy
stories.summary: Latitude Media reports that the election was a repudiation of rising costs, with energy 'indisputably on the ballot' as gasoline and electricity price anger helped flip governorships in Ohio, Nevada and elsewhere, with winners pledging new data-center restrictions and ratepayer protections.

stories.headline: Voters approve dozens of anti-data center ballot measures
stories.summary: Canary Media says Democrats who campaigned against data center buildouts swept congressional and governor's races while voters approved more than 30 local measures aimed at reining in the power-hungry facilities, with the Senate now set to vote Nov. 9 on permitting reform.

stories.headline: Democratic state wins open door to tougher utility and data-center rules
stories.summary: Canary Media notes Democrats flipped governorships in Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas and won full legislative control in five more states, positions that could let them push utilities and data centers toward cleaner power and lower costs.

stories.headline: Major utilities signal no change to data-center-driven spending plans after election
stories.summary: Utility Dive reports Duke Energy is holding its $103 billion, gas-heavy spending plan steady despite the 'historic' election outcome, while Sempra separately expects a 20% jump in Oncor's capex tied to load growth and DTE is expanding its investment plan 30% by selling an unregulated unit.

stories.headline: Berkshire Hathaway's Pacific Power seeks historic 57% California rate hike
stories.summary: WSJ reports Pacific Power is asking California regulators to approve a 57% rate increase that would raise the typical residential bill by $120 a month.

stories.headline: 'Simply staggering' super El Niño on track to peak in December
stories.summary: Carbon Brief reports a rapidly developing 'super El Niño' is likely to peak at the end of 2026, pushing average global temperatures sharply higher.

stories.headline: China's quarterly CO2 emissions fall 3%, largest drop since Covid
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's analysis finds China's CO2 emissions fell 3.1% in the third quarter of 2026, linked in part to the ongoing Hormuz crisis's economic effects.

stories.headline: US solar manufacturing booms but supply-chain gaps remain
stories.summary: Canary Media reports U.S. factories can now produce more finished solar panels than needed for annual installations, but weaker links persist further up the supply chain, with Rhodium Group modeling wide uncertainty for post-2030 installation levels.

Energy.gaps: E&E News could not be checked directly since its coverage has moved behind POLITICO Pro and no recent standalone articles were found; Argus Media had no retrievable recent coverage. Reuters, FT, WSJ, NYT and The Economist could only be reported via provided feed items since they block web search.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across Chinese, Taiwanese and Western outlets centers on diplomatic maneuvering ahead of the November 18-19 APEC summit in Shenzhen, including prospects for a historic Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting, alongside heightened Taiwan Strait military tensions and Hong Kong's ongoing political crackdown following Joshua Wong's sentencing. Business and tech outlets are tracking China's AI race (Apple-Alibaba partnership, domestic model launches) and signs of economic strain requiring central bank intervention.

stories.headline: China confirms discussions for historic Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting
stories.summary: Beijing's foreign ministry confirmed for the first time it is discussing a potential three-way summit between Xi, Trump and Putin on the sidelines of the APEC meeting in Shenzhen this month, though experts say the leaders are unlikely to discuss substantive issues given diverging interests.

stories.headline: Report suggests PLA may be simulating Taiwan isolation in major unannounced exercise
stories.summary: A joint report from the American Enterprise Institute and Institute for the Study of War said China may be running an undeclared exercise larger than last year's drills, with over 100 PLA Navy and coast guard vessels detected in two concentrations around Taiwan and toward Guam.

stories.headline: Taiwan closes Papua New Guinea office, citing Chinese coercion
stories.summary: Taiwan said it has decided to close its representative office in Papua New Guinea and withdraw staff, blaming Chinese pressure on the South Pacific nation for the move.

stories.headline: China's Communist Party vows 'zero tolerance' on election meddling ahead of party congress
stories.summary: China's ruling party has warned of zero tolerance for bribery and interference attempts as delegate selection begins for next year's 21st national congress.

stories.headline: Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years, drawing foreign condemnation
stories.summary: Jailed pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 years after pleading guilty to colluding with foreign forces, with Hong Kong officials hailing the ruling while foreign governments and NGOs condemned it.

stories.headline: China's central bank pledges more support to stabilize stock markets
stories.summary: PBoC Governor Pan Gongsheng outlined plans to draw in long-term investment and reinforce state investor Central Huijin's role as a market stabilizer, following a pullback in major mainland stock indexes.

stories.headline: Apple's rocky partnership with Alibaba powers China AI rollout
stories.summary: Apple Intelligence began beta testing in China on Nov. 4 with Alibaba's Qwen model powering select Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence features, capping what has been a bumpy partnership.

stories.headline: US approved Nvidia chip access for Chinese firms with murky backgrounds
stories.summary: The report describes how the US Commerce Department cleared dozens of Chinese companies to handle Nvidia's H200 chips, including some with ties to sanctioned entities and reportedly empty offices.

China.gaps: Could not retrieve any recent coverage from China Media Project, Rest of World, Sixth Tone, Yicai Global, or ChinaTalk; Reuters, AP, FT (beyond feed), WSJ and The Economist block search so only feed items were used for FT/NYT.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Middle East outlets are overwhelmingly focused on the intensifying US-Israel-Iran war, with fresh US strikes, an expanded blockade and Iranian threats dominating live blogs, alongside Israel's deepening political crisis as Netanyahu battles efforts to oust him. Humanitarian suffering in storm-battered Gaza, Saudi-Syria-Yemen security dynamics, and Gulf economic data on budgets, inflation and oil markets round out coverage.

stories.headline: US expands Iran blockade as Trump confirms new strikes, IRGC lifts missile-range limit
stories.summary: US Central Command is launching a new task force to restrict Iran's movement of weapons and sanctioned goods across land borders and the Caspian Sea, building on a naval blockade that CENTCOM says has already blocked over $25 billion in Iranian crude exports, while Iran's Revolutionary Guard announced it has lifted its self-imposed 2,000km missile-range cap and Trump confirmed a fresh 'minor' strike on an Iranian air-defense site near Qeshm Island.

stories.headline: Israel's political crisis deepens as opposition gains ground against Netanyahu
stories.summary: Israel's opposition said it was making headway in its bid to oust Prime Minister Netanyahu after a key leader lifted his veto on demands that ultra-Orthodox Jews serve in the military, as Netanyahu called for a unity government days after Trump moved to cut US military aid to Israel.

stories.headline: Heavy rains flood tens of thousands of displaced people's shelters in Gaza
stories.summary: Palestinian authorities said heavy weekend rains flooded tents housing tens of thousands of displaced people across Gaza, leaving families without shelter, while the Palestinian health minister warned of a looming disease outbreak amid aid shortages hampering the response.

stories.headline: Syria denies sending troops to Yemen as Saudi military ties deepen
stories.summary: A Syrian diplomatic source dismissed reports of a planned troop deployment to Yemen even as Khaleej Times cited sources telling AFP that Syrian troops were set to deploy in Yemen and Saudi Arabia, underscoring deepening but contested Syrian-Saudi military cooperation.

stories.headline: Saudi budget deficit widens on falling oil revenue despite non-oil resilience
stories.summary: Saudi government revenue reached roughly $229 billion in the first nine months of 2026 while spending rose faster, as oil revenue slipped 1% but non-oil revenue climbed 8%, widening the kingdom's fiscal gap even as unemployment fell and the PMI signaled continued private-sector growth.

stories.headline: UAE businesses raise prices at record pace amid rising costs
stories.summary: UAE businesses raised prices at a record pace in October as firms passed higher operating costs on to customers, a closely watched survey found, raising concerns about emerging inflation in the non-oil economy.

stories.headline: Abu Dhabi property transactions jump 76% to Dh171bn in first nine months of 2026
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi's real estate market recorded a sharp 76% jump in transaction value to Dh171 billion in the first nine months of 2026, pointing to continued strength in the emirate's property sector despite regional tensions.

stories.headline: Oil settles below $100 as Hormuz tensions persist and diplomats seek breakthrough
stories.summary: Brent crude settled at $98.32 a barrel and WTI at $90.83 as markets weighed prospects for diplomatic progress, even as Qatar pushed proposals to bridge US-Iran differences over the nuclear program and Hormuz shipping restrictions.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not find recent (last 24-48h) coverage from Arabian Business, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, The New Arab, or Ynetnews; Reuters, AP, NYT and BBC block search and had no relevant feed items provided.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage this week is dominated by South Africa's bruising municipal elections and the ANC's historic decline, Tanzania's politically charged conviction of opposition leader Tundu Lissu, and the fallout from Washington's decision to strip South Africa and Rwanda of AGOA trade privileges. Business and mining outlets are focused on strong Q3 earnings from African gold and platinum producers, Dangote's regional energy expansion, and Nigeria's tightening fintech/crypto regulation.

stories.headline: ANC suffers historic losses in South Africa's municipal elections
stories.summary: Early results showed the ANC falling to about 32% of the vote with the DA in second place, a sharp decline that could trigger complex coalition battles in major metros like Johannesburg and Durban. African Business noted the party was bracing for its lowest-ever vote share, while Africa Confidential's cover story examines the political cost of the ANC's grip on power.

stories.headline: Tanzania's Tundu Lissu convicted of incitement, cleared of treason
stories.summary: A Dar es Salaam court sentenced opposition leader Tundu Lissu to four years in prison for incitement but dismissed the capital treason charge, a case that had drawn international condemnation as politically motivated. His Chadema party called the dismissal of the death-penalty charge a partial victory even as rights advocates say it shows the prosecution's real goal was simply to jail him.

stories.headline: US strips South Africa and Rwanda of AGOA trade benefits
stories.summary: Washington will suspend both countries from duty-free access under the African Growth and Opportunity Act from January 2027, citing trade barriers, corruption and human rights concerns, affecting roughly $1.7bn of South African exports. African Business reports South Africa's exclusion follows deepening tensions with Washington over its ICJ genocide case against Israel and visa restrictions targeting South African officials.

stories.headline: Somalia's political crisis deepens after court blocks president's term extension
stories.summary: Somalia's opposition accuses the president of sending troops to arrest the Supreme Court's chief justice after the court declared his attempted term extension unlawful, escalating a constitutional standoff.

stories.headline: Namibia's president takes personal control of Dangote's $2.5bn fuel project
stories.summary: President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah says she will personally oversee Dangote's fuel storage and regional pipeline project, determined not to let bureaucracy derail another major investment. Al Jazeera separately reported on the launch of the Namibian fuel storage facility as part of Dangote's push to secure Southern Africa's fuel supply.

stories.headline: Ethiopia's rebased $201bn economy brings bigger tax bill, not easier borrowing
stories.summary: Addis Ababa says the rebasing confirms Ethiopia as sub-Saharan Africa's third-largest economy, but economists say the bigger GDP figure mainly benefits tax collection rather than growth or credit access. Africa Confidential separately reports that the government's economic push coincides with escalating conflict in the country's north, threatening to undercut the investment narrative.

stories.headline: African gold and platinum miners post strong Q3 results
stories.summary: AngloGold Ashanti is targeting organic growth of over 400,000 oz a year by 2029 while reaffirming full-year guidance, and Sibanye-Stillwater reported higher quarterly earnings across its South African platinum and gold operations, reflecting a strong run for the sector amid elevated gold prices.

stories.headline: Nigeria's central bank tightens rules on crypto peer-to-peer payments
stories.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria's new rules require every P2P crypto transaction to be linked to a bank transaction, part of a broader push to gain greater visibility into crypto trading as Nigeria also rewrites its cybersecurity laws to counter AI-driven fraud.

Africa.gaps: Could not find recent, distinct coverage from The Continent, or from Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ (these outlets block search and no relevant feed items were supplied for them).

Media.overview: Media-industry outlets are converging on a major press-freedom story out of the Trump White House alongside blockbuster business news in streaming consolidation and AI-driven disruption of the news business. Trade press is also processing how newsrooms covered the midterms, continued fallout from UK media trials, and new legal fronts in the AI copyright wars.

stories.headline: White House and DOJ reportedly discussed jailing journalists to unmask leakers
stories.summary: Citing an Atlantic report on Susie Wiles' exit as chief of staff, Mediaite reports that the DOJ has reportedly been discussing potentially throwing journalists in jail to reveal the identities of leakers, with new chief of staff Stephen Miller endorsing the idea while Wiles pushed back; a DOJ spokesperson called the account "absolutely false."

stories.headline: Fox Corp. completes $22 billion acquisition of Roku
stories.summary: Fox closed its $22 billion purchase of Roku, folding it into a new Fox Digital Platforms unit alongside Tubi, Fox One and Red Seat Ventures, a combination Adweek notes makes Fox the third-largest entity in U.S. TV by viewing share with access to more than 100 million streaming households.

stories.headline: USA Today Co. blames AI disruption for weak earnings, but also bets on it
stories.summary: Poynter reports the largest U.S. newspaper chain posted a lackluster third quarter — including a net loss and declining revenue — while pointing to AI as both a cause of its struggles and a potential fix going forward.

stories.headline: Meta shelves controversial terms of service after backlash
stories.summary: Nieman Lab reports Meta has indefinitely delayed proposed commercial terms of service that would have permitted the company to scrape the websites of Meta Business account users.

stories.headline: Elvis and Eminem rightsholders sue AI music generator Suno
stories.summary: Variety reports that Elvis Presley music rightsholders and Eminem's publisher filed sprawling new federal lawsuits against AI music generator Suno, escalating the entertainment industry's legal fight against generative AI tools.

stories.headline: Russell Brand's guilty verdict seen as vindication for journalism amid courtroom hostility
stories.summary: Press Gazette reports that journalism came under direct attack during the trial — including a defence barrister swearing at a Sunday Times reporter outside court — before being vindicated by the guilty verdict.

stories.headline: Piers Morgan's production company swings to a loss after News UK exit
stories.summary: Press Gazette reports Piers Morgan's Wake Up Productions moved into the red, with revenue falling by £11.6 million after Morgan's exit from News UK, even as the company maintains big ambitions.

stories.headline: Newsrooms and anchors reflect on a historic midterms election-night performance
stories.summary: CJR examines how election night coverage played out, including a head-to-head between Steve Kornacki and Hasan Piker and Trump calling into coverage, as part of a broader round of outlets assessing midterms journalism.

Media.gaps: No fresh (last 24-48h) media-industry stories could be found for Status or Puck via search; both outlets' most recent located content was weeks old. NYT, WSJ, FT and The Guardian block search, and no media-industry-relevant feed items from those outlets were provided (their feed items concerned unrelated geopolitics/lifestyle topics).
